newsitem.title: CHINA: U.S. businessman jailed in China considers appeal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. businessman jailed in China considers appeal.

text.p: A U.S. businessman sentenced this week by a Chinese court to 10 years in jail for illegally importing garbage is considering an appeal, his lawyer said on Thursday.

William Ping Chen, 56, was sentenced by a Shanghai court on Monday to 10 years in jail, deportation and ordered to pay a 500,000 yuan ($60,000) fine after he confessed to smuggling 238 tonnes of garbage and medical waste into Shanghai in 1995.
"He is considering whether or not to appeal the sentence now," said lawyer Yuan Jiyu. "According to the law, he has 10 days from the day of the sentence to decide."
Yuan said he could not speculate on when Chinese authorities would carry out the deportation order against Chen, who was born in Shanghai but now has a home in Oakland, California.
U.S. diplomats have said they were checking with Chinese officials on whether Chen would need to serve part or all of his sentence before being deported.
A U.S. consular spokesman said he had no further information on the case.

Chen was arrested in June last year and sentenced following an open hearing on December 2 attended by an official from the U.S. consulate in Shanghai. The official Xinhua news agency said he confessed to the charges.

Chen's arrest was the climax of an emotional campaign launched by China in mid-1996 over illegal shipments of U.S. garbage listed as waste paper for recycling but found to contain old clothes, rubber gloves, and disposable syringes.

Chen had listed the imports as waste paper and mixed paper, and proceeded with the shipments despite warnings from Shanghai environmental officials and opposition from his Chinese joint venture partners, Xinhua said.
